examples.solution_text:
Use millimetres for both quantities.
$91\text{ mm}:14\text{ cm}=91:140$
The HCF is $7$.
$91:140=(91\div7):(140\div7)=13:20$

(a) Use cents: $\$4.35=435$c.
$435:75=(435\div15):(75\div15)=29:5$
(b) Use days: $2$ weeks $=14$ days.
$14:9$ has no common factor greater than $1$, so it is already simplest.
Keep the larger-unit quantity first in both ratios.

Use millimetres for all three parts.
$65\text{ cm}:1.4\text{ m}:250\text{ mm}=650:1400:250$
The HCF of all three is $50$.
$650:1400:250=(650\div50):(1400\div50):(250\div50)=13:28:5$

examples.question_text: Lina writes $5$ L $:350$ mL as $1:70$. Explain the error and simplify the original ratio correctly.
examples.solution_text:
Lina simplified $5:350$ without making the units the same.
$5\text{ L}:350\text{ mL}=5000:350$
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}5000:350\\&=(5000\div50):(350\div50)\\&=100:7\end{aligned}$
Converting first preserves the actual comparison.

Use minutes: $3\text{ h}=180\text{ min}$.
The HCF of $180$ and $75$ is $15$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}180:75\\&=(180\div15):(75\div15)\\&=12:5\end{aligned}$

(a) Use grams: $0.9\text{ kg}=900\text{ g}$.
The HCF is $300$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}900:600\\&=(900\div300):(600\div300)\\&=3:2\end{aligned}$
(b) Use millilitres: $1.2\text{ L}=1200\text{ mL}$.
The HCF is $150$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}450:1200\\&=(450\div150):(1200\div150)\\&=3:8\end{aligned}$
